newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on long liquidation.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended lower on Monday compared to New York's previous close after a late bout of shortcovering failed to recover earlier losses on long liquidation, bullion dealers said.
"It's a bit of a mystery, why gold is so low," said one bullion dealer.
Bullion ended at US$346.20/70 an ounce against New York's US$346.60/347.10 close on Friday.
Long liquidation in early trade pushed gold down, compounded by selling from Australia and from Japan.
Dealers said that the strong U.S. dollar had made gold markets nervous, and noted the metal had been capped at $349 per ounce for a week, exacerbating bearishness.
Support was seen at $345.50 to $346 per ounce, but dealers said gold was likely to test lows overnight.
Some dealers said weak stock markets should help gold, but others noted that this could be when funds sought bargains in stocks, pulling out of gold.
Local gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,208 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +1.00 from its previous fix at -5.00.
